reason.description: Why this may be closed WITHOUT an observed recovery. Twenty characters is the floor because a one-liner is not a justification for dismissing an open operational condition.

tenantId.description: Platform-side: restrict the run to one tenant

allowRiskReducingOrders.description: Whether triggered (automatic) protections admit risk-reducing orders. Manual kill switches are ALWAYS total halts; this flag cannot open them.

reason.description: Why the version is being withdrawn from replay use. Stored verbatim in the audit record and mirrored to dataset storage; never truncated in the DB copy.

deviceId.description: Must match the device the refresh token was issued to.

reason.description: Why the release is rejected (recorded verbatim in the audit)

reason.description: Requested operator reason, audited alongside the job. Ingestion is a storage and bandwidth decision; "why now" belongs in the record.

sourceKind.description: Which historical source to read. Only public/local sources ship; a source kind that could carry credentials is not accepted, at the type level.

note.description: What was found and what was done about it.

reason.description: Reason recorded in the audit trail.

priority.description: Tie-break priority; lower wins among equal values

target.description: Scope target: venue id, account uuid, strategy uuid or SYMBOL. Absent ONLY for GLOBAL.

value.description: The ceiling as an exact decimal string; floats are rejected.

windowMicros.description: Rate rules only: window micros, exactly 1000000 or 60000000.

targetReleaseId.description: Explicit previous release to restore; omit for the latest eligible

changeReason.description: Why the rollback is happening (>= 20 chars)

enabled.description: True to enable the account for trading, false to disable it.

makerFeeRate.description: Maker fee RATE, not bps. 0.001 is ten bps.

parameters.description: Strategy parameters. Validated against the version parameter schema.

slippageBps.description: Slippage in basis points against every taker fill.

strategyId.description: Run against an existing instance, inheriting its venue, symbol and parameters. Provide either this or definitionKey + version.

reason.description: Reason recorded in the audit trail.

password.description: Initial password for the tenant owner.

isSecret.description: Store the value encrypted and never return it in plaintext.

value.description: Arbitrary JSON value. Encrypted at rest when isSecret is true.

customCss.description: Custom CSS. Rejected with 400 when it contains @import, remote url(), expression() or markup; accepted CSS is additionally sanitised server-side.

socialLinks.description: Map of social network to profile URL.

preferences.description: Preferences to store. Security-critical notifications are always delivered regardless of these settings.

annotations.description: Reserved for future policy bags; credential-screened

changeReason.description: Why this revision exists. Required because "never silently modify a risk limit" is the clause this whole endpoint exists to enforce.

confirm.description: Required when the revision WIDENS any effective ceiling relative to the current one (the service detects this and refuses without the phrase).

feeRateBps.description: Authoritative fee rate (bps) used by the fee-budget estimate. Absent means the fee rule refuses rather than guesses; it is never defaulted.

notes.description: Free-form note carried in the document (max 500)

priceDeviationReference.description: Reference the deviation band measures against. Default SIDE_TOUCH.

permissionKeys.description: Replaces the full permission set when provided.

badEvent.description: The counting rule for a bad sample, in words.

description.description: What the objective means, for whoever reads it at 3am.

enabled.description: Enablement. Flipping it never changes the checksummed identity of the objective (the version bumps; the promise does not).

goodEvent.description: The counting rule for a good sample, in words.

latencyThresholdMicros.description: Latency-compliance indicators: the compliance threshold in microseconds (integer string).

maxAgeMicros.description: Freshness indicators: the age budget in MICROSECONDS as an integer string. Forbidden on count indicators; required on freshness ones.

shortWindowMinutes.description: Short (paging) window in minutes, inside the long window.

reason.description: Reason recorded in the audit trail.

isGlobalDefault.description: Value applied when a tenant has no override.

message.example: Must be a valid email address

artifactId.description: Artifact id to re-verify from bytes

challengeToken.description: Challenge token returned by the login endpoint.

deviceId.description: Must match the device used in the login request.

trustDevice.description: Remember this device for future sign-ins.

configuration.description: Requested white-label configuration (free-form, stored on the request).

reason.description: Reason recorded in the audit trail (disable).

info.description:
Multi-tenant crypto copy-trading platform API

## Multi-tenancy
Every request is bound to exactly one organisation. For authenticated calls the tenant is read
from the `tid` claim of the access token and a client-supplied tenant identifier can never
override it. For unauthenticated calls the tenant is resolved from the custom domain, then the
platform sub-domain, then the `x-tenant-slug` header.

## Response envelope
Successful responses are wrapped as `{ "success": true, "data": ..., "meta": { "requestId", "timestamp" } }`.
Errors are wrapped as `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details", "requestId", "timestamp", "path" } }`.
Stack traces are never returned outside development.

## Authentication
Bearer access tokens are short lived. Refresh tokens rotate on every use and are bound to a
device; presenting a consumed refresh token revokes the entire token family and signs the user
out everywhere.

## Rate limiting
Two buckets are enforced: a generous default bucket and a strict bucket on authentication
endpoints. Exceeding either returns 429 with `Retry-After`.

get.description: The merged evaluation of the nine platform trading gates: market data, risk engine, risk snapshot freshness, venue connectivity, execution adapter, reconciliation, queues, kill switches and configuration. Fail-closed by construction - missing or stale evidence reads as NOT ready, never as ready. This endpoint has no influence on the risk gate; an order is refused by checks the engine itself runs, regardless of anything said here. Always 200: the verdict lives in the body, because an endpoint that goes 503 when honestly reporting "not ready" invites the orchestrator to kill the messenger during exactly the outage it is describing.
